chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Yahya ibn Amr ibn Khalifa al-Zayyat, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from one of our companions, from one of the two (peace be upon them), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O group of youths! It is upon you to use the marital relationship (al-bah). So if you are not in a position to do so, upon you is with the Fasting, for it is its subduer.'

key_terms.الصِّيَامِ: Fasting, prescribed here as a spiritual and physical discipline to curb desires.
key_terms.الْبَاهِ: The marital relationship or sexual intercourse, used here as a means of satisfying natural desires.
key_terms.وِجَاؤُهُ: Its subduer or controller, referring to fasting's role in controlling sexual desire.

ai.seo_question: What is the prophetic advice for young men who cannot marry regarding fasting and marital relations?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in al-Kafi, establishes fasting as a spiritual and physiological discipline for youth to curb sexual desire when marriage is not immediately attainable. Shia scholars often contextualize 'al-bah' as sexual intercourse, viewing this advice as a practical prophetic strategy for maintaining chastity and emotional stability during the transitional years before marriage. The recommendation highlights the complementary nature of physical satisfaction and ascetic restraint in Islamic ethics.
